cards.text: Ezekiel, a priest living among the exiles (Ezekiel 1:1-3), gets another word from the LORD. God calls him "Son of man" and tells him to prophesy against the prophets of Israel. These prophets are busy prophesying, but their messages aren't coming from God.

cards.question: The prophets of Israel aren't getting their messages from God. God says they prophesy out of their own ___.
God calls these prophets wise for following their own spirit.

cards.text: God calls them foolish prophets who follow their own spirit "yet have seen nothing." Imagine leaving a FIVE-STAR review for a hotel you never checked into.
Then God paints a picture: Israel's prophets are like foxes among the ruins. Not the comparison you want on your business card, friend.

cards.question: God says these prophets went up to the gaps and restored the wall around the house of Israel.
Why did the wall around the house of Israel need restoring?

answers.text: So it would stand in battle on the Day of the LORD
So it would stand through the famine the LORD sends
So it would stand when the LORD brings the exiles home

cards.text: These prophets see false visions and speak lying divinations, then claim, "Thus declares the LORD," when the LORD did not send them. Like telling everybody you got the job when nobody EVER called you back.

cards.question: The LORD did not send these prophets. Even so, what do they do with their message?

answers.text: They wait for it to be fulfilled
They admit that they made it up
They stop telling it to anyone

cards.text: Waiting on a message the LORD never sent? That's sitting by the door for a package you NEVER ordered.
Then God asks them, "Haven't you seen a false vision and spoken a lying divination when you proclaim, 'Thus declares the LORD,' even though I have not spoken?"

cards.question: Because of their vain words and false visions, what does God tell these prophets?
God says the false prophets won't be recorded in the register of the house of Israel.

cards.text: No seat in the council of His people, and no entering the land of Israel either. God says, "Then you will know that I am the Lord GOD."
God's not done with these prophets yet: they led His people astray. Listen to what they told them.

cards.question: What word did the false prophets tell God's people, even though it wasn't true?

cards.text: "Peace," when there is no peace. Your GPS says NO TRAFFIC AHEAD while you haven't moved in twenty minutes.

cards.question: When somebody builds a flimsy wall, these prophets ___ it.

cards.text: Whitewash on a flimsy wall is like sprinkles on a burnt cookie, baker. Looks GREAT, still burnt.

cards.question: God tells Ezekiel to tell the whitewashers that their wall will stand.
What does God say will come against that whitewashed wall?

cards.text: Then God says, "Surely when the wall has fallen, you will not be asked, 'Where is the whitewash with which you covered it?'" Nobody stands in a pile of rubble admiring the paint job.
This storm comes from God Himself. In His wrath He'll release a windstorm, and in His anger torrents of rain and hail will fall with destructive fury.

cards.question: God says He will level the whitewashed wall to the ground, so its foundation is exposed.
When the whitewashed wall comes down, what else does God say will fall?
After the wall is gone, God says the prophets who whitewashed it will still be around.

cards.text: After His wrath, God says, He'll tell them the wall is gone, and so are the prophets who whitewashed it. Those are the prophets who saw a vision of peace for Jerusalem when there was no peace.
Now God points Ezekiel to another group: the daughters of his people. They prophesy out of their own imagination too.

cards.question: God tells Ezekiel to leave these women alone and say nothing to them.

cards.text: God says woe to the women who sew magic charms on their wrists and make veils for the heads of people of every height.

cards.question: Why do these women make the magic charms and the veils?

cards.text: Then God asks them, "Will you ensnare the souls of My people but preserve your own?" Leaky umbrellas for everybody else, and the good one tucked under your OWN arm.

cards.question: God says these women profaned Him among His people. What did they do it for?

answers.text: Handfuls of barley and scraps of bread
Pieces of silver and bars of gold
Fine linen robes and gold jewelry

cards.text: Handfuls of barley and scraps of bread, baker. The expired coupon I shared a junk drawer with offered better deals than THAT.

cards.question: God says these women's lies spared those who should not have lived.

cards.text: These women's lies also killed those who should not have died, God says. So He's against the magic charms they use to ensnare souls like birds.

cards.question: What does God say He'll do with the souls these women trapped like birds?

cards.text: God says He'll tear the charms from the women's arms and tear off their veils, so His people won't be prey in their hands anymore. Charms OFF. Veils OFF. Nobody's prey anymore.

cards.question: God says these women disheartened the ___ with their lies and encouraged the ___ not to turn from their evil ways.
How much grief does God say He caused the people these women disheartened with their lies?

cards.text: God says these women will no longer see false visions or practice divination. Then He says, "I will deliver My people from your hands. Then you will know that I am the LORD."
